content: Hi, I run a small clinic and I want a system so patients can book appointments with our doctors online.
Happy to help. Who will be using this system? For example, just patients, or your clinic staff as well?
Both. Patients book their own appointments, and my front desk staff need to manage the doctors and see all the bookings.
Got it. What do you need to know about each patient when they sign up?
Their full name and phone number for sure. Email and date of birth would be nice but not everyone has an email.
Makes sense, so name and phone are required, email and date of birth are optional. Can two patients share the same phone number?
No, each patient should have their own number. We use it to find them.
Thanks. What should we store about each doctor?
Their name, what they specialise in, like general practice or paediatrics, and a contact phone if they have one. Only staff should be able to add, change or remove doctors.
Understood. When a patient books, what details go with the appointment?
Which doctor, the date and time, and a short reason for the visit if they want to give one. Each appointment is 30 minutes.
Are there any rules about when someone can or can't book?
A doctor can't have two appointments at the same time, obviously. And you shouldn't be able to book something in the past.
Good rules. If a patient can't make it, should they be able to cancel the appointment themselves?
Yes, patients should be able to cancel. We'd like to keep a record of cancelled ones rather than deleting them.

Here's what I have. A clinic appointment system used by patients and clinic staff. We store patients (full name, phone, optional email and date of birth; phone is unique), doctors (name, specialty, optional phone) and appointments (patient, doctor, start time, optional reason, status). Patients register, see doctors, book 30-minute appointments and cancel them. Staff add, edit and remove doctors and see all patients and appointments. Rules: no overlapping appointments for the same doctor, no bookings in the past, and cancelled appointments are kept, not deleted. Does that look right?
